projects.title: Projects
projects.lead: Selected work, 2024 → now. Most of it runs in production — some under NDA, so code links are private.
projects.caseStudyPending: The full case study is being written. Until then, this is the short version.

tgPlus.title: TG+
tgPlus.description: Georeferenced inventory, remote management and reporting for city lighting. Operators see every luminaire on a live map, schedule dimming and get alerted when one fails — usually before anyone on the street notices.
tgPlus.role: My part: built the frontend from scratch, own the TALQ integration and contribute to the .NET IoT services.

module.label: module
module.name: TALQ integration
module.description: Lets third-party city platforms bootstrap, read data from, control and group our luminaires through the international TALQ API: calendars, control programs, scheduled overrides, and pushed measurements and alerts.

frontend.title: Frontend from scratch
frontend.body: React/TypeScript architecture with layout, routing, contexts, an API layer and standardized tables. Leaflet maps (KMZ, GeoServer heatmaps, region drawing), real-time updates over WebSocket STOMP, PDF/XLSX reports, pt-BR/es translations and a NextUI → HeroUI migration.

talq.title: TALQ integration
talq.body: Gateway side of the open TALQ protocol: bootstrap, device classes and devices, commissioning, calendars, control programs, override commands scheduled with JobRunr, log reports pushing measurements and alerts, mTLS and per-deployment tiers. ~8.9k lines of code and ~5.4k of tests.

commands.title: Remote commands that adapt to the device
commands.body: In the frontend, buttons and tabs change with the modem's technology and firmware, with bulk sends, multicast and dimming. In the backend and the .NET core, new DLMS commands: Cellular Identity, Heart Beat Extended and Link Check Interval.

units.title: Lighting units with slots and history
units.body: Domain remodel that keeps history when a photocell is swapped, with dual-write and a resolver feeding ~12 aggregated endpoints. Backend and frontend, feature-gated per environment.

observability.title: Observability in the .NET services
observability.body: /health endpoints in 6 services checking MQTT, RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ and Redis without opening new connections per request, structured logging with ILogger in the connectors, and a migration to .NET 8.

map.label: Map of a street grid with connected luminaires lighting up

experience.title: Experience
experience.lead: Where I've shipped code. Read it like a git log — newest on top.

bullets.frontend: Architected TG+'s React/TypeScript frontend from scratch and wrote ~76% of today's code (~53k lines): Leaflet and GeoServer maps, real-time updates over WebSocket (STOMP), PDF/XLSX reports and pt-BR/es translations
bullets.talq: Designed and built the TALQ open-protocol integration on my own, in Java/Spring Boot: ~9k lines, 200+ tests, mTLS, JobRunr scheduling and per-city feature flags
bullets.commands: Built config-driven remote commands, single and bulk, that adapt to each device's technology and firmware, and added new DLMS/COSEM commands to the .NET core
bullets.units: Remodeled the lighting-unit domain to keep history when hardware is swapped, with dual-write and aggregated endpoints, from database to UI
bullets.connectors: Maintain the .NET IoT connectors: added health checks (MQTT, RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ, Redis) and structured logging to 6 services, and migrated them to .NET 8
bullets.adrs: Wrote 12 of the backend's 31 architecture decision records (ADRs)
